changes.description: Updated C10's memo to reflect that CCDC 14 is the first reviewed form that constitutes a genuine single-point Design-Build consolidation: Article A-1.1/A-1.2 assigns both Design Services and the Work to a single 'Design-Builder,' and GC 3.1.1-3.1.9 makes the Design-Builder solely responsible for design, construction means/methods, and for the acts/omissions of the Consultant and Other Consultants it engages under a CCDC 15 design-services subcontract.
changes.justification: The research lens identifies single-point DB/EPC consolidation as a key MMC-enabling delivery structure; CCDC 14 provides the clearest positive instance among reviewed forms (contrasted with the traditional DBB/CM forms previously reviewed where the code did not apply), making it essential to document this instance for cross-form comparison.

changes.description: Updated C17's memo to record that CCDC 14 GC 3.1.7 and GC 12.3.1 explicitly set the Design-Builder's responsibility for Consultant/Other Consultant design services at a 'reasonable skill and care' standard ('degree of care, skill and diligence normally provided by consultants...in respect of projects of a similar nature'), rather than a fitness-for-purpose standard, and limit liability to negligent performance covered by professional liability insurance.
changes.justification: CCDC 14 is the first reviewed form in which the Contractor-side entity actually assumes design responsibility, making it the clearest available comparator for the standard-of-care question the code targets; the explicit clause language directly resolves the ambiguity the code is designed to capture.

changes.description: Updated C18's memo to note that CCDC 14 situates Shop Drawing review responsibility entirely within the Design-Builder's own organization: the Design-Builder reviews and represents completeness/co-ordination of Shop Drawings before submission (GC 3.10.3), Owner review is optional and, when conducted, is limited to conformity with contract intent and general arrangement only (GC 3.10.4-3.10.5), and such review does not relieve the Design-Builder of responsibility for Shop Drawing errors.
changes.justification: Because CCDC 14 consolidates design and fabrication administration under one entity, it provides a distinct comparator to the CM and DBB forms for how design-to-fabrication handoff liability is allocated when no independent Owner-side Consultant reviews shop drawings by default.

changes.description: Updated C19's memo to note that while GC 1.1.2 preserves the traditional privity-denial structure (no contractual relationship between Owner/Consultant and Subcontractors/Suppliers), CCDC 14 nonetheless consolidates the Consultant, Other Consultants, Subcontractors and Suppliers as parties engaged directly by the Design-Builder (GC 3.1.3, GC 3.4.1), re-centering the expanded stakeholder network under a single contracting entity rather than the Owner.
changes.justification: This clarifies how stakeholder-role consolidation under MMC-relevant delivery models varies with the design-build structure specifically, complementing the CM-based comparators already documented for this code.

changes.description: Updated C22's memo to record that CCDC 14 provides materially stronger off-site QA/inspection hooks within the primary agreement itself: GC 3.1.10 requires the Design-Builder to provide access to 'parts being performed at locations other than the Place of the Work,' and GC 2.2.5 confirms the Owner's authority to require inspection or testing of work 'whether or not such work is fabricated, installed or completed.'
changes.justification: These clauses closely parallel the strongest off-site access/inspection provisions previously identified in CCDC 5B, confirming that design-build delivery, like CM-at-Risk, can support more robust off-site fabrication QA than the DBB baseline, which is directly relevant to the literature's emphasis on traceability/certification of prefabricated components.

changes.description: Updated C24's memo to note that CCDC 14 GC 3.4.1-3.4.5 establishes a Design-Builder-intermediated supply chain (the Design-Builder itself contracts with Other Consultants, Subcontractors and Suppliers) subject to Owner objection rights before signing, with Contract Price/Time adjustment where the Owner requires a change of proposed party (GC 3.4.3-3.4.4), closely mirroring the CCDC 3/CCDC 5B pattern of Owner pre-approval over subcontract selection layered onto a contractor/CM-intermediated architecture.
changes.justification: This provides a design-build-specific data point for comparing supply chain coordination/risk-transfer architectures across delivery models, relevant to how manufacturer/fabricator engagement is structured and who bears the cost of Owner-directed substitutions.

changes.description: Updated C14's memo to note that CCDC 14 Part 8 (GC 8.1.1-8.1.10) omits the 'Consultant finding' first step present in CCDC 2/CCDC 3/CCDC 5B, proceeding directly from negotiation to mediation to arbitration; this is consistent with the Consultant being a party engaged by (and answerable to) the Design-Builder rather than serving as an independent Owner-side adjudicator of disputes.
changes.justification: This confirms and extends the code's existing finding (from CM forms) that the presence/absence of an independent first-instance adjudicator in the dispute escalation ladder tracks the administrative/organizational position of the Consultant relative to the parties, a useful comparator across delivery models relevant to MMC dispute risk.

changes.description: Updated C28's memo to note that CCDC 14, despite consolidating design and construction into a single Design-Builder entity, still relies on GC 1.1.6's Supplementary Conditions priority mechanism as the sole vehicle for introducing MMC/prefabrication-specific terms (e.g., off-site storage insurance, fabricated-Products payment recognition, design-freeze timelines), and its Article A-5/GC 5.2.3 payment mechanics remain delivery-gated in the same manner as the DBB and CM forms reviewed.
changes.justification: This confirms the meta-level structural gap persists even in the design-build delivery model most naturally suited to consolidating fabrication risk, reinforcing the code's cross-form applicability.

codebook.label: Payment Timing Misaligned with Off-Site Production
codebook.definition: Clause provisions governing progress payment certification based on on-site inspection/completion or delivery to the Place of the Work, which do not accommodate value created through off-site fabrication prior to delivery or installation.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses defining what work/value is payable in a progress payment (e.g., 'Work performed and Products delivered to the Place of the Work') where off-site fabrication progress is not a recognized basis for payment.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely defining the Products/Materials term itself (use C2), holdback/retention mechanics (use C4), or fee-for-service payment clauses in agency CM forms where compensation is not tied to Products/Work value at all (see C33).
codebook.memo: Combines T3, T4, T8, T10, T11, T13, T14 codes on 'work done vs work due'. In CCDC 2 (and CCDC 2 CcQ), GC 5.2.3/5.2.8 tie payment to delivery at the Place of the Work. In CCDC 3, GC 5.3.3/5.3.7 reproduce the same delivery-gated logic despite the Cost of the Work definition reimbursing off-site shop labour as a direct cost. CCDC 5B GC 5.4.3 reproduces the identical delivery-gated formula, confirming this misalignment recurs in the CM-at-Risk cost-reimbursable structure. In CCDC 5A, GC 4.1.1-4.1.3 base the CM's own progress payment on the earned amount of the CM's compensation for Services, not on Products delivered. CCDC 14 GC 5.2.3 ('value...of the Design Services and of the Work performed and Products delivered to the Place of the Work') reproduces the identical delivery-gated payment formula within a Design-Build agreement, confirming the misalignment recurs even where design and fabrication are consolidated under one entity.

codebook.label: Ambiguous Definition of 'Products'/Materials for Prefabricated Modules
codebook.definition: The contractual definition of Products/materials incorporated into the Work is unclear as to whether it covers fabricated but undelivered or uninstalled modules, creating payment-claim ambiguity.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses defining 'Products' or equivalent terms and clauses referencing Products for payment purposes without addressing off-site fabricated/stored modules.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely governing payment timing/certification procedure (use C1).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 3.7.3 defines Products generically; GC 5.2.3/5.2.8 tie Products to delivery, not off-site fabrication. CCDC 3 does not define Products distinctly from the base form. CCDC 5B GC 3.7.2 similarly requires Products to be new/quality-consistent but does not define Products in relation to off-site fabricated status. CCDC 5A contains no equivalent Products definition. CCDC 14 GC 3.8.2 similarly requires Products to be new/quality-consistent without addressing off-site fabricated/stored status, and GC 5.2.8 only addresses evidentiary support for Products delivered but not incorporated, leaving fabricated-but-undelivered status unaddressed, consistent with the baseline gap.

codebook.label: Advance Payment and Upfront Financing Provisions
codebook.definition: Contract clauses addressing advance payments, deposits, or financing arrangements to reflect MMC's front-loaded capital requirements for design, fabrication and materials.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses providing for deposits, advance payments, or Owner financing assurances relevant to funding pre-delivery fabrication costs.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general Owner financial-capacity disclosure clauses that do not create an advance-payment mechanism (still flag as a notable absence, but tag rather than treat as satisfying the code).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 5.1 and CCDC 3 GC 5.1.1-5.1.2 only require evidence of Owner financial arrangements. CCDC 5A GC 3.1.1.7 and CCDC 5B GC 5.1.1-5.1.2 reproduce the identical financing-evidence-only mechanism. CCDC 14 GC 5.1.1-5.1.2 reproduces the same financing-evidence-only mechanism ('furnish...reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made'); no advance payment mechanism exists for Design Services or fabrication costs, confirming the gap recurs even in a Design-Build form with front-loaded design/fabrication cost exposure.

codebook.label: Statutory Retention/Holdback and Liquidated Damages Provisions for Off-Site Work
codebook.definition: Clauses governing statutory or contractual retention (holdback/security) amounts—whether structured as lien holdback, legal hypothec holdback, or other security-of-payment mechanism—and liquidated damages clauses, which may need adjustment or removal to reflect MMC's reduced on-site activity and front-loaded cost structure.
codebook.include_when: Apply to holdback/retention clauses of any statutory form (construction lien holdback, legal hypothec holdback, etc.) and any liquidated damages clauses, including their release mechanics.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses governing progress payment valuation generally (use C1).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 5.4 and CCDC 3 GC 5.6-5.7 set out holdback mechanics tied to Work/Product value. CCDC 5A A-6.1 requires holdback applied to the Construction Manager's fee-based compensation. CCDC 5B GC 5.6.1-5.6.6/A-11.1 ties holdback to the value of the Work/Cost of the Work. CCDC 14 GC 5.5-5.6 reproduces the CCDC 2/3 holdback and progressive-release mechanics tied to the value of Design Services and Work/Products, again with no liquidated damages clause in the General Conditions, consistent with the recurring pattern across all reviewed forms.

codebook.label: Insurance and Payment Security for Modules in Transit/Storage
codebook.definition: Provisions extending insurance coverage and payment security to prefabricated components during off-site storage and transportation, addressing gaps in standard care-of-work clauses.
codebook.include_when: Apply to insurance clauses (property, transit, builder's risk) whose scope is unclear or silent regarding off-site storage/transit of prefabricated Products.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general liability or workers' compensation insurance clauses unrelated to Products/materials risk.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 11.1.1.4 and CCDC 3 GC 11.1.1.4 scope Broad Form property insurance to the Work at/near the Place of the Work with no off-site storage/transit coverage. CCDC 5A GC 8.1.2.1 sizes property insurance limits to include Owner-supplied Products value. CCDC 5B GC 11.1.1.4 reproduces the base scoping. CCDC 14 GC 11.1.1.5 similarly scopes 'all risks' property insurance to the Work from commencement of the Work until near Substantial Performance, with no dedicated off-site storage/transit coverage regime for fabricated modules; the added professional liability insurance requirement (GC 11.1.1.9) addresses design-error risk but not off-site Products risk, confirming the gap persists in the Design-Build form.

codebook.label: Contingency/Change-Order Funding for Post-Fabrication Scope Changes
codebook.definition: Clauses providing mechanisms and compensation for scope changes or variations occurring after fabrication has commenced, recognizing the high cost of altering already-produced components.
codebook.include_when: Apply to contingency allowance clauses and change valuation clauses insofar as they address (or fail to address) the elevated cost of altering already-fabricated MMC components.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to routine change order procedural clauses with no bearing on fabrication-stage cost impact (use C9).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 4.2 and CCDC 3 GC 4.1 provide generic contingency/cash allowance mechanisms not tailored to post-fabrication change costs. CCDC 5B GC 4.1.1-A to 4.1.7-A reproduce the same generic mechanism. CCDC 5A contains no contingency allowance clause. CCDC 14 GC 4.2.1-4.2.4 reproduces the same generic contingency allowance mechanism valued through ordinary Change Order/Change Directive procedure, not tailored to the elevated cost of altering already-fabricated MMC components.

codebook.label: Dynamic/Rebate-Based Delivery Schedule Compensation
codebook.definition: Mechanisms (surcharges, rebates, incentives) that adjust compensation based on real-time cost impacts of delivery-date changes between contractor and off-site supplier/fabricator, as an alternative to fixed compensation.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses creating variable/dynamic compensation tied to delivery schedule changes vis-à-vis a fabricator/supplier.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard delay/extension of time clauses that do not involve schedule-based compensation adjustment mechanisms (use general delay provisions, uncoded unless MMC-specific).
codebook.memo: Not found in CCDC 2 CcQ or CCDC 3. CCDC 5A GC 5.1.4 and CCDC 5B GC 6.5.1-6.5.3 provide only standard Contract Time extension/cost-adjustment mechanisms. CCDC 14 GC 6.5.1-6.5.5 likewise provides only standard delay/extension-of-time and cost-reimbursement mechanisms with no dynamic/rebate-based delivery compensation mechanism; absence is a valid, recurring result. Combines T1, T4, T5, T6 codes on dynamic compensation and rebate mechanisms.

codebook.label: Design Freeze and Change-Control Timing Requirements
codebook.definition: Clause provisions requiring early finalization of design before fabrication and governing the cost/schedule consequences and approval timelines for changes made after design freeze.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses mandating or implying a design-freeze point or setting timelines for design decisions/approvals relevant to fabrication commencement.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general Shop Drawing review clauses absent any design-freeze/fabrication-timing linkage.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ has no explicit design-freeze clause; CCDC 3 GC 3.10 matches. CCDC 5A's A-5.5 and CCDC 5B's A-5.2 termination-compensation scale reflect estimate maturity stages rather than a design-freeze requirement. CCDC 14's GC 2.5.1-2.5.4 (Owner's review of design development documents and proposed Construction Documents, with a 10-day acceptance/rejection timeline) governs design review timing but does not establish a design-freeze point after which fabrication may proceed without further design change; this remains a notable, recurring absence, now also confirmed in the Design-Build form best positioned to benefit from an explicit freeze mechanism.

codebook.label: Variation/Change Order Procedures and Valuation Methods
codebook.definition: Clauses specifying procedures, valuation methods, notice/time-bar requirements, and scope limitations for pricing and approving variations, particularly relevant where MMC's fixed design conflicts with flexible on-site change processes.
codebook.include_when: Apply to Change Order/Change Directive/claims-for-change clauses describing process, valuation basis, or notice/time-bar requirements.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply where the clause solely concerns contingency allowance funding (use C6).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 6.2-6.3 and CCDC 3 GC 6.2-6.3 provide detailed cost-based valuation for Change Directives. CCDC 5A GC 5.1.1-5.1.5 provides a comparatively thin change process. CCDC 5B GC 6.2-6.3 values Change Directives on a cost-based methodology matching CCDC 3. CCDC 14 GC 6.1-6.3 reproduces the same cost-based Change Directive valuation (actual expenditures/savings plus percentage fee, GC 6.3.6-6.3.7), confirming this valuation methodology recurs in the stipulated-price Design-Build form as well.

codebook.label: Single-Point Design-Build/EPC Responsibility Consolidation
codebook.definition: Contractual structures consolidating design, procurement, and construction (including fabrication) responsibility into a single entity (EPC/DB/manufacturer-builder), shifting risk from owner and enabling constructability/manufacturing input.
codebook.include_when: Apply to articles/clauses establishing a single-point design-and-build responsibility structure.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to traditional DBB forms with separate Consultant/Contractor roles unless a specific consolidation clause is present.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ and CCDC 3 are traditional Design-Bid-Build/cost-plus forms; this code does not apply. CCDC 5A is a CM-Advisor (agency) form with a fragmented structure. CCDC 5B's Construction Manager consolidates construction/subcontract responsibility but design remains the Consultant's separate responsibility, a partial construction-side consolidation only. CCDC 14 is the clearest positive instance reviewed to date: Article A-1.1/A-1.2 assigns both Design Services and the Work to a single 'Design-Builder,' and GC 3.1.1 ('total control of the Design Services and of the Work'), GC 3.1.3-3.1.4 (Design-Builder must contract with the Consultant under CCDC 15 terms), and GC 3.1.6 (Design-Builder as fully responsible for Consultant/Other Consultant acts and omissions as for its own employees) together establish a genuine single-point design-build responsibility structure, directly matching the code's definition and providing the strongest available comparator for MMC-enabling consolidated delivery models.

codebook.label: Multi-Party/IPD Shared Risk-Reward Provisions
codebook.definition: Contractual mechanisms in multiparty/IPD agreements formalizing shared risk and reward, incentive compensation pools, liability caps/waivers, and collaborative behavioral commitments among owner, designer, contractor and manufacturer.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses establishing shared risk/reward pools or multiparty collaborative commitments.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard bilateral indemnification/waiver clauses (use C15), or to bilateral Owner-Construction Manager cost-savings-sharing mechanisms within a GMP option (use C32).
codebook.memo: Not present in CCDC 2 CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, or CCDC 5B (all bilateral agreements, with CCDC 5B's GMP savings-sharing option coded under C32 instead). CCDC 14 is likewise a bilateral Owner-Design-Builder agreement with no multiparty/IPD shared risk-reward pool; absence remains a valid, expected result across all reviewed CCDC forms to date.

codebook.label: Early Contractor/Manufacturer Involvement Mechanisms (ECI/PCSA/Two-Stage)
codebook.definition: Provisions enabling and compensating early involvement of contractors, manufacturers, and suppliers in design through two-stage tendering, preconstruction services agreements, or Alternative Technical Concepts, including timing of engagement.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses providing for early contractor/manufacturer design input, preconstruction services, or two-stage procurement, including fee-structured Pre-Construction Phase service categories that compensate a Construction Manager or contractor for design-stage advisory involvement prior to trade/fabrication contract award.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard Shop Drawing review (GC 3.8/3.10), which occurs after Contract award, not pre-award/early design input.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ and CCDC 3 assume Contractor engagement after design completion with no ECI/PCSA mechanism. CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B establish genuine, compensated ECI/preconstruction-services mechanisms. CCDC 14 does not fit this code despite involving contractor-side design responsibility: the Design-Builder performs the full Design Services itself under Article A-1.1 rather than providing early advisory input into an Owner-led design process; there is no separate Pre-Construction Services fee category or two-stage procurement mechanism. This is a distinguishable delivery concept (full design-build consolidation, coded under C10) rather than early involvement in a design still controlled by others, and its absence here is valid and expected.

codebook.label: Termination and Suspension Rights Clarity
codebook.definition: Clauses defining the parties' rights, obligations, notice requirements, and discretion regarding suspension and termination, addressing ambiguity that is a recurring dispute driver.
codebook.include_when: Apply to default notice, termination, and suspension clauses defining triggering events, cure periods, and consequences.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to dispute resolution procedural clauses (use C14).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ Part 7 and CCDC 3 Part 7 provide detailed reciprocal termination/suspension procedures. CCDC 5A Part 6 and CCDC 5B Part 7 provide estimate-maturity-scaled and hybrid termination-compensation models respectively. CCDC 14 Part 7 (GC 7.1-7.3) reproduces the reciprocal DBB-style termination/suspension structure, with termination compensation for Owner-initiated termination based on the full cost of finishing the Design Services and Work (GC 7.2.5.4) rather than an estimate-maturity scale, and Design-Builder-initiated termination compensation including 'reasonable profit' (GC 7.3.6) — a straightforward reciprocal model without the estimate-class scaling seen in the CM forms, reflecting the fixed stipulated-price basis of CCDC 14.

codebook.label: Dispute Resolution Escalation and Cost-Efficiency
codebook.definition: Tiered dispute resolution provisions (negotiation, mediation, arbitration/litigation) and their cost-efficiency, including proactive checklists to reduce dispute-inducing ambiguity.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses establishing dispute escalation steps (Consultant finding, negotiation, mediation, arbitration/litigation).
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses defining Consultant's general interpretive authority absent a dispute-escalation mechanism (use general administration, uncoded).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ Part 8 and CCDC 3 Part 8 establish tiered Consultant-finding/negotiation/mediation/arbitration structures. CCDC 5A Part 7 omits the Consultant-finding first step, reflecting the CM's non-adjudicative agency role. CCDC 5B Part 8 restores the Consultant-finding step. CCDC 14 Part 8 (GC 8.1.1-8.1.10) omits the Consultant-finding first step entirely, proceeding directly from negotiation to mediation to arbitration, consistent with the Consultant in this form being a party engaged by and answerable to the Design-Builder (GC 3.1.3) rather than an independent Owner-side adjudicator — confirming that the presence/absence of a first-instance Consultant-finding step tracks the Consultant's organizational independence from the party seeking to rely on it, a useful comparator across delivery models for MMC-related dispute risk.

codebook.label: Risk Allocation Fairness and General Conditions Balance
codebook.definition: How the general conditions document allocates risk between owner and contractor across cost, schedule, quality, safety and environmental objectives, and whether this allocation is balanced or unilaterally biased toward the owner.
codebook.include_when: Apply to indemnification, waiver-of-claims, liability limitation, and broad risk-allocating clauses.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to narrow procedural clauses (e.g., notice mechanics) unless they materially affect risk allocation outcomes.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 13.1/13.2 and CCDC 3 GC 12.1/12.2 reflect reciprocal risk allocation models. CCDC 5A GC 10.1-10.3 caps liability against the Fee for Services. CCDC 5B GC 13.1-13.3 caps liability against the greater of the full Contract Price or $2,000,000. CCDC 14 GC 12.2.2.2 reproduces the CCDC 5B-style Contract-Price-based cap ('greater of the Contract Price...or $2,000,000, but in no event...greater than $20,000,000'), while also adding a distinct GC 12.3.1 limitation of liability specifically for Design Services (tied to available professional liability insurance) — illustrating how a design-build form layers a design-specific liability limitation onto the standard construction risk-allocation architecture, a significant comparator for MMC projects combining large fabrication cost exposure with contractor-borne design risk.

codebook.label: Particular Conditions/Bespoke Amendment Effects
codebook.definition: How supplementary/particular conditions and bespoke modifications to standard forms add clarifying detail, introduce inconsistency, or alter risk balance relative to unmodified general conditions.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses referencing Supplementary Conditions or particular conditions and their interaction/priority with General Conditions.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply where no supplementary/particular conditions mechanism is referenced.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ A-3.1/GC 1.1.5 and CCDC 3 A-3.1/GC 1.1.7.1 establish Supplementary Conditions with defined priority. CCDC 5A GC 1.1.1.1 and CCDC 5B GC 1.1.5.1 reproduce the mechanism. CCDC 14 GC 1.1.6.1 reproduces the identical mechanism, placing Supplementary Conditions between the Definitions and the General Conditions in the priority order, confirming this is the consistent vehicle across all reviewed forms through which MMC-specific bespoke amendments would be introduced.

codebook.label: Design Liability Standard: Fitness-for-Purpose vs Reasonable Skill and Care
codebook.definition: Clause language determining whether a party assuming design responsibility (e.g., contractor/manufacturer under design-build/MMC) is held to a fitness-for-purpose standard or a reasonable skill and care standard.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses assigning design responsibility and specifying (or leaving ambiguous) the applicable standard of care.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply where the Contractor bears no design responsibility under the form (as under pure DBB).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ and CCDC 3 assign design responsibility to the Consultant/Owner side except delegated Temporary Work design. CCDC 5A GC 2.1.3 and CCDC 5B GC 1.5.1 disclaim CM responsibility for the Consultant's professional design responsibilities. CCDC 14 is the first reviewed form in which the Contractor-side entity (the Design-Builder) actually assumes design responsibility, making the standard-of-care question directly operative: GC 3.1.7 expressly limits the Design-Builder's responsibility for Design Services performed by the Consultant/Other Consultants to 'the degree of care, skill and diligence normally provided by consultants in the performance of comparable services in respect of projects of a similar nature' — an explicit reasonable-skill-and-care standard, not fitness-for-purpose — and GC 12.3.1 reinforces this by limiting the Design-Builder's liability for Design Services claims to those arising from negligent performance, capped at available professional liability insurance (GC 11.1.1.9). This provides the clearest positive data point yet for comparing design liability standards across delivery models.

codebook.label: Design-Fabrication Liability Allocation Across Delivery Models
codebook.definition: How liability for digital fabrication/manufacturing errors arising from design-information handoff is allocated among general contractor, designer, and fabricator, and how this varies by delivery model (DBB, DB, CM, IPD).
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses addressing responsibility for errors arising from the handoff of design information to fabrication (e.g., Shop Drawings).
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general defective work clauses unconnected to a design-to-fabrication handoff issue.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 3.8 and CCDC 3 GC 3.10 allocate Shop Drawing review responsibility to the Consultant (design-concept conformity only) with the Contractor retaining error responsibility. CCDC 5A contains no Shop Drawing review clause; CCDC 5B GC 3.8.1-3.8.7 restores a full Shop Drawing regime with the Construction Manager reviewing and representing completeness. CCDC 14 GC 3.10.1-3.10.5 situates Shop Drawing review entirely within the Design-Builder's own organization: the Design-Builder reviews and represents completeness/co-ordination of Shop Drawings (GC 3.10.3) before optional submission to the Owner, whose review (if requested) is limited to conformity with contract intent and general arrangement only (GC 3.10.4-3.10.5) and does not relieve the Design-Builder of responsibility for errors — providing a design-build-specific comparator in which the design-to-fabrication handoff occurs largely internally to a single consolidated entity, materially reducing the cross-party handoff risk the code targets relative to DBB/CM models.

codebook.label: Scope of Work, Roles, and Multi-Manufacturer Reference Clarity
codebook.definition: Clauses defining scope of work and the roles/responsibilities of an expanded set of stakeholders (manufacturers, fabricators, suppliers), including provision for referencing or sourcing across multiple manufacturers.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses defining stakeholder roles/relationships, especially where MMC introduces additional parties (manufacturers/fabricators) beyond the traditional Owner-Consultant-Contractor triad.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely addressing Subcontractor/Supplier selection procedure without role-definition ambiguity (use C24).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 1.1.6 and CCDC 3 GC 1.1.2 expressly deny privity between Owner/Consultant and Subcontractors/Suppliers. CCDC 5A formalizes an expanded multi-party stakeholder structure via separate CCDC 17 Trade Contracts. CCDC 5B reverts to the traditional privity-denial structure. CCDC 14 GC 1.1.2 similarly denies privity between the Owner and the Consultant, Other Consultants, Subcontractors or Suppliers, but the Design-Builder itself directly engages and coordinates all of these parties (GC 3.1.3, GC 3.4.1) as part of a single consolidated contracting entity — re-centering the expanded stakeholder network (including manufacturers/fabricators engaged as Subcontractors/Suppliers or Other Consultants) under the Design-Builder rather than the Owner, a distinct architecture from both the CM-Advisor (Owner-direct) and CM-at-Risk (partial consolidation) models previously documented.

codebook.label: BIM Contractual Status: Model Authority, Ownership and Liability
codebook.definition: Contract provisions establishing whether the BIM model or 2D drawings govern, ownership/licensing of model data, liability for reliance on the model, and required BIM Execution Plans/coordination roles.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses addressing BIM model precedence, ownership, licensing, or reliance liability.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to generic drawing/specification ownership clauses that do not address digital model status specifically, unless clearly extending to BIM.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 1.1.10/1.1.11 and CCDC 3 GC 1.1.9/1.1.10 address general ownership of drawings/models without BIM-specific precedence. CCDC 5A contains no ownership-of-documents/models clause. CCDC 5B GC 1.1.10/1.1.11 reproduces the general ownership language. CCDC 14 GC 1.1.7-1.1.10 reproduces comparable general copyright/ownership language for plans, sketches, Drawings, 'electronic media' and 'computer generated designs' prepared on behalf of the Design-Builder, but without any BIM-specific precedence, ownership, or reliance-liability provision; absence of BIM-specific treatment remains a valid, recurring result even in the Design-Build form where an integrated digital model would be most useful.

codebook.label: Smart Contract/Automated Payment and Performance Verification Clauses
codebook.definition: Provisions enabling blockchain/smart-contract-based automation of progress payments and incentive/penalty enforcement, including oracle verification, governance, and limits requiring human oversight for unforeseen events.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses referencing automated/algorithmic payment or verification mechanisms.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard Consultant-certification payment clauses.
codebook.memo: Not present in CCDC 2 CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, or CCDC 5B, all relying on traditional certification processes. CCDC 14 likewise relies on a traditional Payment Certifier-administered process (GC 2.4, GC 5.3) with no automated/algorithmic mechanism; absence is expected and valid across all reviewed forms.

codebook.label: Quality Assurance, Certification and Inspection of Off-Site Products
codebook.definition: Clauses specifying certification models (self-certification vs third-party), inspection requirements, and chain-of-custody/traceability obligations for prefabricated modules and components.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses on testing/inspection/certification that extend, or could extend, to off-site fabricated work, including access rights to off-site fabrication locations.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to on-site-only inspection clauses with no bearing on off-site fabrication.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 2.2.11/2.3.1 and CCDC 3 GC 2.2.12/2.3.1 provide limited hooks for off-site QA/access. CCDC 5A contains no equivalent clause. CCDC 5B provides materially stronger hooks via GC 2.4.1 and GC 2.3.11. CCDC 14 provides comparably strong hooks within the primary agreement itself: GC 3.1.10 requires the Design-Builder to 'provide access to the Work, including parts being performed at locations other than the Place of the Work,' and GC 2.2.5 confirms the Owner's authority to require review of the Design Services and inspection or testing of the Work 'whether or not such work is fabricated, installed or completed' — closely paralleling the CCDC 5B off-site access/inspection regime and confirming that stronger off-site QA hooks are a feature of both integrated CM-at-Risk and Design-Build delivery models relative to the DBB baseline.

codebook.label: Transportation, Logistics, and Site Access Risk Allocation
codebook.definition: Clauses addressing risk, cost, and regulatory constraints for transporting oversized/heavy prefabricated modules and coordinating site access/vertical logistics, including insurance during transit.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses addressing transportation cost/risk or site access/logistics coordination for Products/modules.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general Products procurement cost clauses without a transportation/logistics dimension.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 6.3.7.2 and CCDC 3 A-4.1.2 reference transportation cost as a change/cost-of-the-work line item. CCDC 5A contains no equivalent reference. CCDC 5B's Cost of the Work definition explicitly itemizes transportation of Products and expediting labour. CCDC 14, as a stipulated-price form, includes 'transportation' generically among the Design-Builder's own-cost obligations under GC 3.8.1 and among chargeable Change Directive cost elements (GC 6.3.7), but does not itemize transportation/expediting costs as a distinct reimbursable category the way the cost-reimbursable CCDC 3/CCDC 5B forms do; this is consistent with the fixed-price basis of CCDC 14 and is a valid, informative contrast.

codebook.label: Supply Chain Coordination and Subcontractor Risk Transfer
codebook.definition: Provisions governing how risk, cost savings, and coordination burdens are distributed between main contractor, subcontractors, manufacturers and suppliers, including onerous subcontract terms, logistics service mandates, and Owner approval rights over Subcontractor/Supplier selection.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses governing Subcontractor/Supplier/Trade Contractor engagement, flow-down obligations, risk transfer mechanisms, or Owner pre-approval/change rights over proposed Subcontractors/Suppliers/Trade Contractors, including direct Owner-Trade Contractor contracting structures administered by an agent Construction Manager.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses solely defining stakeholder roles/definitions without a risk-transfer or coordination dimension (use C19).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 3.6 and CCDC 3 GC 3.7.1-3.7.3 establish a Contractor-flow-down risk-transfer baseline, with CCDC 3 adding Owner approval rights. CCDC 5A presents an Owner-direct contracting model via CCDC 17. CCDC 5B GC 3.6.1-3.6.3 reverts to a CM-intermediated architecture with Owner bid-acceptance rights. CCDC 14 GC 3.4.1-3.4.5 establishes a comparable Design-Builder-intermediated architecture: the Design-Builder itself contracts with Other Consultants, Subcontractors and Suppliers (GC 3.4.1) and must disclose proposed parties to the Owner on request (GC 3.4.2), the Owner may object for reasonable cause before the subcontract is signed and require a different party (GC 3.4.3), with Contract Price/Time adjusted for the resulting differences (GC 3.4.4) — a design-build-specific instance of the Owner pre-approval/change-right pattern previously documented for CCDC 3 and CCDC 5B, extending the comparator set to the design-build model and confirming this architecture recurs regardless of whether the intermediating entity is a Contractor, CM, or Design-Builder.

codebook.label: Incentive/Subsidy Pass-Through and Revenue-Sharing Contract Structures
codebook.definition: Contractual mechanisms (revenue-sharing, fixed transfer payments, reward-penalty) distributing government subsidies or incentives between developer, contractor, and supplier to encourage higher prefabrication uptake.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses distributing subsidies/incentives among parties.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general tax/duty pass-through clauses unrelated to prefabrication incentive policy (use general tax clauses, uncoded).
codebook.memo: Not present in CCDC 2 CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A, or CCDC 5B; all address only general tax pass-through. CCDC 14 GC 10.1.1-10.1.2 likewise contains only a general tax/duty pass-through mechanism with no subsidy-distribution provision; absence is a valid, recurring result across all reviewed forms.

codebook.label: Environmental Responsibility Allocation Clauses
codebook.definition: Contractual provisions distributing environmental compliance responsibility between contractor and off-site supplier, often shaped by government reward-penalty or subsidy policy mechanisms.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses allocating environmental compliance responsibility specifically in relation to off-site supply/fabrication.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general hazardous-substance/mould clauses addressing on-site conditions only (those relate to site environmental risk, not off-site supplier responsibility allocation policy).
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 9.2/9.5 and CCDC 3 GC 9.2/9.5 address on-site environmental risk only. CCDC 5A contains no such clause; CCDC 5B GC 9.2/9.5 reproduce the on-site-only regime. CCDC 14 GC 9.2/GC 9.5 similarly reproduce the full on-site-only toxic/hazardous substances and mould regime found in the other forms; off-site supplier environmental responsibility allocation remains absent, a valid and consistently recurring result.

codebook.label: Product-Based/Framework Contracting for Modular Systems
codebook.definition: Alternative procurement structures treating modular buildings as standardized products with fixed long-term supplier agreements or framework/serial contracts, rather than one-off project contracts.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses establishing framework/serial or product-based procurement structures.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard single-project stipulated-price or cost-plus agreements.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B are all single-project agreements with no framework/product-based procurement structure. CCDC 14 Article A-1.2 likewise describes a single named Work/Project with no framework/serial or product-based procurement structure; absence is a valid, expected result across all reviewed forms.

codebook.label: Absence of Dedicated MMC/MOC Standard Contract Forms
codebook.definition: The recognized gap that no standard contract form is designed specifically for modular/off-site construction, requiring adaptation of conventional forms (e.g., CCDC) and resulting in ambiguity and increased dispute/litigation risk.
codebook.include_when: Apply as a meta-level/whole-form observation when a form's overall structure (payment, Products definition, inspection, insurance) shows no MMC-specific adaptation, requiring reliance on Supplementary Conditions.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to individual clause-level gaps already captured by more specific codes (C1, C2, C5, C22, etc.); use this code for the overarching structural observation only.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ's and CCDC 3's reliance on Supplementary Conditions exemplifies this meta-level gap. CCDC 5A displaces most fabrication-related administration to unreviewed CCDC 17 Trade Contracts. CCDC 5B reintegrates several off-site-relevant provisions but still relies on Supplementary Conditions as the sole vehicle for bespoke MMC terms. CCDC 14, despite consolidating design and construction responsibility into a single Design-Builder entity (the delivery model arguably best positioned to internalize MMC coordination), still relies on GC 1.1.6's Supplementary Conditions priority mechanism as the sole vehicle for introducing MMC-specific terms, and its payment mechanics (GC 5.2.3) remain delivery-gated in the same manner as the DBB and CM forms — confirming the meta-level gap persists even in the most construction-and-design-integrated delivery model reviewed to date.

codebook.label: Contract Drafting Clarity and Readability for MMC Terms
codebook.definition: Linguistic and structural quality of contract clauses (grammar, jargon, ambiguity, visual aids) as it affects interpretation of MMC/prefabrication-specific terms and provisions.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses whose drafting quality/ambiguity specifically affects interpretation of MMC-relevant terms (e.g., 'Products', 'Place of the Work').
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to general drafting-quality observations unrelated to MMC/prefabrication terms.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ GC 1.1.7-1.1.9 and CCDC 3 GC 1.1.3-1.1.6 address general interpretive conventions without clarifying MMC-specific terminology. CCDC 5A GC 1.1.2 and CCDC 5B GC 1.1.7-1.1.9 provide comparably minimal interpretive conventions. CCDC 14 GC 1.1.4-1.1.5 provides the same minimal interpretive conventions (technical/trade meanings, singular/plural), with the same absence of MMC-specific terminology clarification across all forms reviewed.

codebook.label: Bundled/Multi-Project Contract Risk Interdependency
codebook.definition: Provisions addressing risk and scheduling interdependency created when multiple projects or sites are bundled under a single contract, including third-party coordination and financing implications.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses expressly addressing bundled/multi-project delivery interdependency.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to standard single-project agreements like CCDC 2 or CCDC 3.
codebook.memo: CCDC 2 CcQ, CCDC 3, CCDC 5A and CCDC 5B are single-project agreements. CCDC 14 Article A-1.2 likewise describes a single Project; absence is a valid, expected result across all reviewed forms.

codebook.label: Cost-Reimbursable Structure's Capture of Off-Site Fabrication Labour and Expediting Costs
codebook.definition: Provisions within cost-reimbursable (cost-plus) Cost of the Work definitions that explicitly recognize off-site shop labour, expediting, and transportation activity as direct, reimbursable cost categories, independent of whether Products have been delivered to the Place of the Work.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses defining the Cost of the Work (or equivalent reimbursable-cost basis) that include shop-based personnel, expediting, or transportation-related labour/costs as chargeable items.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to clauses governing when such costs may actually be applied for/certified in a progress payment (use C1), or to clauses merely defining Products generically (use C2).
codebook.memo: CCDC 3 Article A-4.1.1(3)/A-4.1.2 reimburses shop-based expediting and transportation as direct costs. CCDC 5A has no Cost of the Work definition of this kind. CCDC 5B Article A-8.1.1(3)/A-8.1.2 reproduces near-identical language. CCDC 14 is a stipulated-price (fixed Contract Price, Article A-4.1) rather than cost-reimbursable form; it has no Cost of the Work definition of this kind, and the code therefore does not apply — its cost-based valuation appears only within the narrower Change Directive mechanism (GC 6.3.6-6.3.7), which is addressed under C9, not C31. Absence is valid and expected given the stipulated-price basis of this form.

codebook.label: Hybrid Cost-Plus/GMP-Target Price Cost-Certainty Mechanisms
codebook.definition: Contractual options layering a Guaranteed Maximum Price, Target Contract Price, or Stipulated Price conversion onto a cost-reimbursable base, providing a middle-ground cost-certainty mechanism between pure cost-plus risk exposure and firm lump-sum pricing, including any associated cost-savings sharing/incentive dimension between Owner and Construction Manager.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses establishing GMP, Target Price, Stipulated Price conversion, or similar hybrid cost-ceiling/incentive mechanisms layered on a cost-reimbursable Contract Price, including their interaction with change valuation, Change Directive costing, and any Owner/Construction Manager cost-savings-sharing formula.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to firm lump-sum stipulated-price agreements with no GMP/Target Price option, to ordinary Change Order/Change Directive valuation mechanics unconnected to a GMP/Target Price ceiling (use C9), or to multiparty/IPD shared risk-reward pools (use C11).
codebook.memo: CCDC 3 Article A-7 establishes an optional GMP/Target Contract Price mechanism. CCDC 5A contains no true GMP/Target Price mechanism. CCDC 5B Article A-10 provides a developed hybrid mechanism including a GMP Plus Percentage Cost Savings option. CCDC 14 is a firm stipulated-price agreement (Article A-4.1) with no GMP/Target Price conversion option; the code does not apply, and this absence is valid and expected given the fixed-price structure of the Design-Build form.

codebook.label: Agency CM Fee-for-Service Compensation Decoupled from Work/Product Cost
codebook.definition: Contractual compensation structures in agency/advisory Construction Management (or similar fee-based) delivery models in which the manager's/consultant's compensation (time-based, fixed, or percentage fee, plus reimbursable expenses) is calculated independently of, and decoupled from, the cost or value of the Work or Products, with the Owner contracting for and paying Work/Products cost directly to Trade Contractors/suppliers under separate agreements.
codebook.include_when: Apply to clauses establishing or applying a fee-for-service compensation basis (time-based, fixed fee, percentage fee) for a construction manager/consultant whose payment is not itself measured by delivered Work/Products value, and to clauses confirming the Owner's direct payment obligation to Trade Contractors/suppliers under separate agreements.
codebook.exclude_when: Do not apply to Contractor/Construction Manager-at-Risk compensation structures where the manager's payment (fee or otherwise) is measured against, or reimburses, the actual cost of Work/Products performed under the same agreement (use C1, C31, or C32 as appropriate).
codebook.memo: CCDC 5A Article A-5 and GC 3.1.1.9 together establish a structural decoupling of CM compensation from Work/Product cost. CCDC 5B is excluded from this code because the CM directly incurs and is reimbursed for Cost of the Work under the same agreement. CCDC 14 likewise falls outside this code's scope: the Design-Builder is paid a single stipulated Contract Price for both Design Services and the Work (Article A-4/A-5), with no fee-for-service compensation decoupled from Work/Product cost and no direct Owner-to-Trade-Contractor/Supplier payment structure; absence is valid and expected, confirming the code's scope remains properly limited to agency/advisory delivery models such as CCDC 5A.
